Answer key positions in this course follow a visible rotation pattern (3,2,1,0,3 / 0,1,2,3,0) per lesson, which may let learners guess.

questions.note: Keyed concept is clear (ill-health concentrated among the poor), but calling that burden 'pro-poor' is nonstandard; conventionally a negative ill-health index denotes inequality unfavourable to the poor.
Choice 2 wording is slightly garbled: second 95 should read '95 percent of those diagnosed on treatment', not '95 percent of those on treatment'.

claims.claim: Under-five deaths fell from roughly 12 million a year around 1990 to under 5 million in recent estimates.
claims.note: UN IGME 2025 report: 4.9 million in 2024; 1990 estimate now about 13 million, so 'roughly 12 million' is slightly low but within the 'approximate' hedge.

claims.claim: Noncommunicable diseases account for roughly three quarters of deaths worldwide by WHO estimates.
claims.note: WHO: 75% of non-pandemic-related deaths in 2021 (at least 43 million).

claims.claim: The Global Burden of Disease study is run by IHME and collaborators; WHO publishes separate Global Health Estimates.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page; consistent with general knowledge.

claims.claim: In the Whitehall studies of British civil servants, mortality rose steadily as employment grade fell, despite stable employment.
The WHO Commission on Social Determinants of Health reported in 2008 as 'Closing the Gap in a Generation'.

CSDH three overarching recommendations: improve daily living conditions; tackle inequitable distribution of power, money and resources; measure and understand the problem and assess the impact of action.
The epidemiologic transition was described by Abdel Omran in 1971, with an age of pestilence and famine, receding pandemics, and degenerative and man-made diseases.
The concentration index ranges from -1 to +1; a negative value means the variable is concentrated among the poor.
claims.note: Standard methodology (Wagstaff/O'Donnell) but not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Worked example: gap 80 before and after, ratio about 2.3 to 5.
claims.note: Arithmetic check: 140/60=2.33, 100/20=5; correct.

claims.claim: Maternal death: death during pregnancy or within 42 days of its end from related or aggravated causes, excluding accidental causes; MMR is per 100,000 live births.
SDG 3 targets: MMR below 70 per 100,000; under-five mortality at most 25 and neonatal at most 12 per 1,000 live births by 2030.
The Three Delays model of Thaddeus and Maine: delay deciding to seek care, reaching a facility, receiving adequate care.
claims.note: Thaddeus & Maine, Soc Sci Med 1994.

claims.claim: The World Health Assembly launched the Expanded Programme on Immunization in 1974; Gavi was created in 2000.
claims.note: EPI via WHA27.57 (1974); Gavi launched Davos, January 2000.

claims.claim: Last natural smallpox case occurred in Somalia in 1977 and eradication was declared in 1980.
GPEI began in 1988; WPV2 and WPV3 certified eradicated; WPV1 remains endemic in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
claims.note: WPV2 declared eradicated Sept 2015, WPV3 Oct 2019. As of Aug 2026 WPV1 still endemic in both (2026: ~19 cases Afghanistan, ~3 Pakistan).

claims.claim: Five Plasmodium species infect humans (falciparum, vivax, ovale, malariae, knowlesi); falciparum most lethal and dominant in Africa, vivax dominant outside.
claims.note: WHO World Malaria Report figures for 2024: ~282 million cases, ~610,000 deaths; African Region ~95%.

claims.claim: Partial artemisinin resistance, first found in Southeast Asia, has been confirmed in parts of East Africa.
claims.note: Confirmed in Eritrea, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania; suspected in Ethiopia, Namibia, Sudan, Zambia.

claims.claim: Two vaccines, RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M, have been recommended by WHO for children.
claims.note: RTS,S 2021, R21 October 2023. (Tu Youyou 2015 Nobel claim not checked: nobelprize.org returned 403.)

claims.claim: Tuberculosis has regained its position as the world's leading cause of death from a single infectious agent.
claims.note: Global TB Report 2025: ~10.7 million ill and 1.23 million deaths in 2024.

claims.claim: MDR-TB is resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin; newer all-oral regimens (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid +/- moxifloxacin) shortened resistant-TB treatment to about six months.
claims.note: BPaLM/BPaL prioritised by WHO in 2022.

claims.claim: Xpert MTB/RIF was endorsed by WHO in 2010 and detects the bacterium and rifampicin resistance within hours.
claims.note: Endorsed December 2010; results in under two hours.

claims.claim: Twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir is a PrEP option as of this writing.
claims.note: WHO guideline recommended LEN PrEP in July 2025; country rollouts (e.g. Kenya, Nigeria) began 2026 with Global Fund procurement.

claims.claim: UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets for 2025: 95% know status, 95% of diagnosed on treatment, 95% of treated virally suppressed.
claims.note: 2024 global: 87-89-95. Targets' 2025 deadline has now passed; UNAIDS has a 2026-2031 strategy, worth noting.

claims.claim: WHO recommends a dolutegravir-based first-line regimen; HPTN 052 showed early treatment sharply reduced sexual transmission.
claims.note: DTG preferred first-line since July 2019; HPTN 052 ~96% interim reduction.

claims.claim: The 2014-2016 West Africa Ebola epidemic caused roughly 28,000 cases and 11,000 deaths.
claims.note: Official totals ~28,600 cases, 11,325 deaths.

claims.claim: A 2015 ring vaccination trial in Guinea vaccinated contacts and contacts of contacts with rVSV-ZEBOV and showed strong protection.
claims.note: Ebola ca Suffit; immediate vs delayed (21 days) clusters.

claims.claim: A randomised trial in DRC found two monoclonal antibody products had lower mortality, and both were later approved.
claims.note: PALM: mAb114 (Ebanga) and REGN-EB3 (Inmazeb), FDA-approved 2020.

claims.claim: IHR amendments adopted in 2024 create a 'pandemic emergency' alert level and are in force for most states, with some having rejected them.
claims.note: In force 19 Sept 2025; 11 of 196 States Parties rejected (incl. US, Italy, Israel, Argentina).

claims.claim: The WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted in 2025 has a pathogen access and benefit-sharing annex still under negotiation.
claims.note: Still under negotiation as of Sept 2026; May 2026 deadline missed, extended to WHA May 2027. Agreement cannot open for signature/enter into force until annex adopted.

claims.claim: 'Announced withdrawal of at least one major member' has prompted WHO budget cuts; most funding is voluntary/earmarked.
claims.note: Wording is stale: the US withdrawal was completed on 22 January 2026 (not merely announced); WHO cut ~22% of staff and 2026-27 budget is $6.2bn. Voluntary = 83% of 2024-25 revenue. Recommend updating text.

claims.claim: The Pandemic Fund, hosted by the World Bank and launched in 2022, provides grants for surveillance, laboratory capacity and workforce in lower-income countries, with demand exceeding funds.
claims.note: Launched at G20 Bali, November 2022.

claims.claim: CEPI's stated aim is a vaccine within 100 days of a threat.
The Global Health Security Index scored countries in 2019 and high scores did not reliably predict COVID-19 performance.
claims.note: Some later analyses find modest associations with excess mortality; 'not reliably' is a fair hedge.

claims.claim: The WHO FCTC, adopted in 2003 and in force from 2005, is the first treaty negotiated under the WHO Constitution.
claims.note: Adopted 21 May 2003; in force 27 Feb 2005.

claims.claim: Cervical cancer elimination 2030 targets: 90% of girls vaccinated by 15, 70% screened with a high-performance test by 35 and 45, 90% treated.

NCDs are about three quarters of global deaths; about three quarters of those occur in LMICs; premature = ages 30-70; SDG target to cut premature NCD mortality by one third by 2030; four shared risk factors.
claims.note: WHO: 75% of non-pandemic deaths; 73% of NCD deaths in LMICs.

claims.claim: The Beveridge model is embodied in the British NHS launched in 1948; the Bismarck model derives from Germany's 1880s sickness insurance law with multiple sickness funds.
claims.note: Sickness Insurance Law 1883.

claims.claim: Taiwan and South Korea are standard examples of single-payer national health insurance.
claims.note: Taiwan NHI 1995; Korea merged funds into a single payer in 2000.

claims.claim: Spain, Nordic countries and New Zealand follow versions of the Beveridge model.
claims.note: Standard textbook classification; not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Thailand's Universal Coverage Scheme, launched 2002, is tax-funded with capitation payments and an initial small copayment.
claims.note: 30-baht copayment initially.

claims.claim: The 2001 Abuja Declaration committed AU members to allocate at least 15 percent of national budgets to health, a target most have not met.
Uganda abolished user fees in public facilities in 2001, with a large rise in attendance but pressure on supplies and staff.
claims.note: Abolished 1 March 2001; drug stock-outs followed.

claims.claim: WHO published its first Model List of Essential Medicines in 1977; the Medicines Patent Pool was set up in 2010 with UNITAID support.
Doha Declaration 2001; a 2003 WTO General Council decision, later a permanent TRIPS amendment, allowed export of compulsory-licensed generics to countries lacking manufacturing capacity.
claims.note: Amendment in force 23 January 2017.

claims.claim: Pharmaceutical companies dropped their challenge to South Africa's 1997 Medicines Act in 2001, and Cipla offered triple therapy at a fraction of prevailing price in 2001.
claims.note: Case dropped 19 April 2001; Cipla offered US$350/year in Feb 2001.

claims.claim: The Declaration of Alma-Ata (WHO/UNICEF, 1978) called for Health for All by 2000; the 2018 Declaration of Astana renewed the PHC commitment.
Selective primary health care was proposed in 1979 by Julia Walsh and Kenneth Warren.
claims.note: NEJM 1 Nov 1979.

claims.claim: WHO projects a shortfall of roughly ten million health workers by 2030; the WHO Global Code of Practice on recruitment (2010) is voluntary.
claims.note: WHO's current projection is 11.1 million by 2030 (largest gaps in African and Eastern Mediterranean regions); 'roughly ten million' reflects the older 2022 figure and could be updated to ~11 million. Code adopted 21 May 2010.

claims.claim: The Belmont Report (1979), produced after Tuskegee, named respect for persons, beneficence and justice; Helsinki first issued 1964.
claims.note: Helsinki most recently revised October 2024.

claims.claim: Peter Lurie and Sidney Wolfe criticised placebo-controlled short-course zidovudine trials in the 1990s.
claims.note: NEJM 1997.

claims.claim: Later Helsinki revisions require testing against the best proven intervention, permitting placebo only when none exists or for compelling scientific reasons without added risk of serious harm.
claims.note: Consistent with para 33 of 2013/2024 text per memory, but I did not open the current Declaration text.

claims.claim: A crude mortality rate above one death per 10,000 people per day is a standard emergency threshold.
claims.note: Sphere/UNHCR prefer doubling of baseline when baseline is known; 1/10,000/day used otherwise.

claims.claim: Medecins Sans Frontieres was founded in 1971 by French doctors and emphasises temoignage (bearing witness).
claims.note: Founded by doctors and journalists. FORMATTING: lesson text has mojibake ('M?decins Sans Fronti?res', 't?moignage') - replacement characters instead of accented letters; needs fixing.

claims.claim: The 1951 Refugee Convention defines a refugee and sets non-refoulement; IDPs are not covered by it.
claims.note: Standard, but not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: GRAM estimated about 1.27 million deaths attributable to and 4.95 million associated with bacterial AMR in 2019.
The 2024 UNGA political declaration set a target to reduce AMR-associated deaths by 10 percent by 2030 against the 2019 baseline.
claims.note: Adopted 26 Sept 2024; also 70% Access-antibiotic target.

claims.claim: mcr-1, plasmid-borne colistin resistance, was discovered in 2015 in animals and humans in China.
claims.note: Liu et al., Lancet Infect Dis, Nov 2015.

claims.claim: Right to health in Article 12 ICESCR (1966); General Comment 14 (2000) set availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality.
The 2005 Paris Declaration on Aid Effectiveness set principles of national ownership, alignment and harmonisation.
claims.note: Five principles incl. managing for results and mutual accountability.

claims.claim: Abrupt reductions in funding by major donors around 2025 disrupted treatment supply and surveillance.
claims.note: Context: Jan 2025 US aid freeze/USAID dismantling; Gavi June 2025 summit raised >US$9bn vs US$11.9bn target; Global Fund 8th replenishment (Nov 2025) ~US$11.3-12.6bn incl. US$4.6bn from US, below prior cycle. Lesson could name these.
